text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging sre-oncall (leo). P99 generation latency spike detected for eu-dedicated pools (pool-eu-22). SLO p99 > 5s for last 10m, p95 drifting up. Auto-scaler shows delayed slot handshake and warmup failures. Please triage — customer-visible streaming stalls reported by a handful of high-throughput tenants.

leo: On it. Can someone paste the graphs and the pool tags? I see alerts firing in ops but need context.

priya: Alerts: /alerts/INC-1790123456 - p99 generation > 5s, queue depth 180 -> 600 in 8m, warmup success rate 40%. Affected model variants: gptx-large-q4a (quantized), fallback to cpu variant not enabled.

maria: Customer support reporting increased timeouts from 3 enterprise customers (eu region). Support ticket IDs: CS-9921, CS-9922, CS-9923. They see streaming stalls (partial frames, resumed on retry).

kevin: Checking infra: autoscaler logs show repeated handshake timeouts to pool-eu-22 nodes. Suspect flux in handshake due to kube-scheduler delays + image pull congestion. Logs:
```
[autoscaler] 2026-03-15T09:12:34Z handshake_timeout pool-eu-22 slot_request_id=ab12c
[runtime] 2026-03-15T09:12:38Z warmup_failed slot_id=slot-94 reason=kv-cache-miss heavy-io
```

leo: Can we confirm whether this is cold KV cache warmup or full model coldstart? Warmup_failed line suggests model started but cache cold. That increases first-token latency.

priya: Both. We've got some slots failing to complete KV prefill in the warmup window because batch cache prefetch is limited per-slot while queue depth exploded. Autoscaler added slots but they didn't reach ready state before traffic hit them.

infra-bot: Current pool-eu-22: desired=45, available_ready=28, initializing=12, failed_init=5. Node image pull latencies spiking in eu-west-3.

leo: Immediate mitigation options: 1) temporarily throttle bursty tenants -> reduce incoming QPS. 2) manual scale of pool with prefilled warmup (force warmup flag) for next slots. 3) enable fallback to smaller model variant (gptx-medium) for streaming endpoints. Which is fastest?

taylor: Support can put soft-rate-limits on the 3 impacted customers if ops asks, but they'd prefer platform-level mitigations to avoid manual per-tenant throttling.

nina: Product: enabling fallback may change output quality. We need to notify those customers if we switch models. Is there a safe automatic fallback policy we can apply for 15m with banner?

kevin: I can do manual scale + force-warmup on new nodes now. That buys us capacity but warmup will still take ~30-60s for KV prefill. If we also enable prefix caching reuse (fast-path) and bump prefetch parallelism to 8 -> we can reduce warmup from ~60s -> ~20s. Doing both now.

leo: Go for manual scale+force-warmup. kevin, please run the scale command and post output. priya, set an SLO advisory and update incident; taylor, craft short customer-safe message ready if we flip fallback.

kevin: Running: 
```
redwood infra scale-pool --pool pool-eu-22 --count 60 --force-warmup=true --warmup-parallelism=8
Request submitted: op-98312. Expected add 15 slots.
```

kevin: infra-bot update: scale op-98312 provisioning 15 nodes, 7 completed warmup, 8 in-progress. 

maria: Support note drafted: "We're observing degraded streaming performance in EU for dedicated capacity customers. We're actively scaling affected pools and may enable temporary quality fallbacks in the next 15-30 minutes. We'll update you with ETA and mitigation steps." Ready to send on your mark.

priya: SLO advisory posted to status page: "P99 latency elevated for eu-dedicated pools. Engineering engaged. Mitigations in progress."

leo: After kevin's warmup bump, are p99/p95 improving? Priya, visual?

priya: Graphs: p95 dropped from 1.8s -> 1.3s after first 7 slots warmed; p99 still at ~3.6s but trending down. Queue depth dropped from 600 -> 230. Streaming stalls reduced but not eliminated.

leo: Good. Keep the manual scale until autoscaler handshake issue is fixed. Need root cause: why were image pulls/handshakes delayed? kevin, can you open a separate infra thread for cluster-level degradations and include the image registry metrics + CNI logs?

kevin: Opening infra thread now: /thread 1790123580 (cluster-registry-pull-lag). Early signal: registry throttling for eu-west-3 region from cloud provider during 09:05-09:18 UTC. We're requesting increased burst capacity.

infra-bot: Failed_inits decreased to 1. Warmup success rate now 88% for newly provisioned slots.

leo: OK — immediate customer impact reduced. Next actions: 1) keep manual scaled pool until autoscaler handshake fix (eng-infra). 2) set temporary global burst throttle policy to smooth onboarding (ops). 3) prepare rollback plan for forced warmup if it causes significant cost. 4) postmortem owner: leo, due EOD.

taylor: Notifying the three impacted customers with the drafted message now. I'm flagging CS tickets and sending an ETA of 30 minutes.

nina: Product wants a follow-up on automatic fallback policy: suggest we add a 'graceful-fallback' feature that preserves quality by routing streaming to warm slots first and only fallback when ETA>15s. Filing feature request FR-4761.

leo: Quick note for postmortem: probable chain: cloud registry throttling -> autoscaler requests delayed -> slots added but image pulls slowed -> warmup window missed for many slots -> queue depth spike -> p99 SLO breach and streaming stalls. We'll verify with logs.

incident-bot: Incident severity set to sev-2. Paging paused. Next update in 20m or on significant change. :white_check_mark:

leo: Thanks team. Keep updates in this thread if anything changes. I'll draft the timeline and initial RCA notes once we confirm registry throttling window.
